summary: Analytics CLI login blocked after Okta email-alias normalization during org alias merge
description:
Issue summary: Several internal engineers are unable to authenticate to the Analytics CLI (internal tool) after last night's Okta org alias migration. The CLI returns a 403 and the support portal shows 'user not found in org' despite the users existing in Okta and having valid sessions.

Impact: ~7 engineers in US-East unable to run ad-hoc queries and deploy debug jobs. No public customer impact, but blocks oncall and incident response for analytics.

Observed behavior: CLI auth flow fails at identity-proxy token exchange with error '400: user_lookup_failed'. Console shows missing runbook links for affected users. Okta shows successful authentication and a SCIM change event for email aliases during the org alias merge window.

Expected behavior: Users with primary or plus-addressing aliases should be mapped to the existing internal account and be allowed CLI login.

Additional context: This started immediately after an Okta org alias merge performed by IdR team (referenced in #okta-org-alias Slack thread) that normalized email aliases and removed legacy externalID suffixes. Affected users share patterns: plus-addressing (+dev) or uppercase letters in aliases that were normalized during the merge.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) User authenticates via Okta OIDC flow from Analytics CLI (v2.3.1)
2) Okta returns ID token and SCIM sync runs for the user (merge event with alias normalization)
3) Identity-proxy receives token and calls internal user-lookup service
4) user-lookup returns 404 due to mismatched external_id mapping after SCIM resync
5) CLI exits with '403 user_lookup_failed' and prints guidance to open a support ticket

investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 04:30 - Triage: Confirmed regression window aligns with Okta org alias merge (IdR change set 2026-03-12-orga-merge).
2026-03-12 05:10 - Support (Nina): Reached out to IdR for SCIM event logs in #okta-org-alias. IdR confirmed bulk normalization of externalID values and removal of '+' characters in externalId policy.

2026-03-12 07:45 - Eng (Liam): Pulled user-lookup DB entries and observed entries indexed by external_id still using pre-merge values (contained plus-signs). SCIM-sync updated Okta side but internal user-index not reindexed for ~20% of users due to a throttled reindex job failing with 429 from our indexer queue.

2026-03-12 08:20 - Hypothesis: Reindex job failure left stale external_id mappings. Identity-proxy normalizes incoming token subject using the new Okta-normalization rules and fails to find a match in our DB. Combined with casefolding differences, lookup misses occur.

2026-03-13 02:00 - Tried manual reindex for a sample user (alice+dev@example.com): reindex succeeded and user-lookup started resolving. Confirmed manual invalidation of user-cache on identity-proxy fixed login for that user.

2026-03-13 09:15 - Discovered CLI v2.3.1 performs lowercase-only normalization on the client side which differs from Okta's normalization (Okta removed non-alphanumeric chars). Mismatch propagate to token external_id claim vs internal DB key.
2026-03-14 10:30 - Runbook test: Simulated full resync in staging and validated sequential flow: scim-sync -> indexer -> identity-proxy cache invalidation -> successful login.

resolution: Mitigation applied: manual reindex of affected external_id ranges and identity-proxy cache invalidation restored access for all impacted users. Root cause: Okta org alias merge changed externalId normalization (strip non-alphanum + lowercase) while our indexer experienced throttled failures leaving stale DB keys that still contained legacy '+' characters. A subsequent mismatch between proxy normalization and Okta's normalization caused lookups to fail. Fixes: 1) Immediate: manual reindex + proxy cache invalidation (completed 2026-03-14). 2) Deployed fix to indexer concurrency defaults (GitHub PR #1528). 3) Created follow-up task to standardize normalization rules across components and add post-SCIM-change verification. Monitoring: login success rate back to baseline in prod/us-east; will monitor for 48 hours.
next_steps: 1) Create durable test in onboarding pipeline to simulate Okta normalization events and verify downstream indexing (owner: Eng - Liam)
2) Add automated post-SCIM resync hook that triggers a reindex sweep for changed external_id prefixes (owner: IdR - Priya)
3) Update Analytics CLI docs and release notes to call out normalization considerations and recommend latest client version (owner: DevEx)
4) Runbook: add 'post-IdR-merge checklist' to Confluence and tag support rotations (owner: SRE)
5) Monitor: keep dashboard alert for user_lookup_404 rate > 0.5% for 24h (owner: SRE)
